name_en: Chagayu — rice simmered thin in roasted tea, Nara's everyday breakfast
summary_ja: 煮出したほうじ茶に冷やご飯を入れてさらりと炊いた奈良の日常食。東大寺のお水取りの献立にも茶粥の原型が記されているとされ、「大和の朝は茶粥で明ける」と言われるほど朝食に根付いている。
summary_en: Cold cooked rice simmered thin in brewed roasted tea, an everyday Nara dish. A forerunner of it is said to appear in the menu for Todai-ji's Omizutori rite, and it is so tied to breakfast that a local saying holds that morning in Yamato begins with chagayu.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Yamato chameshi — rice and soybeans cooked in roasted tea, as eaten by Todai-ji's monks
summary_ja: 米と炒った大豆をほうじ茶で炊き込んだ奈良発祥の飯。東大寺の僧坊で食べられていたものが旅人によって江戸に伝わり、浅草の店で評判になったとされるが、当の奈良では明治以降に改めて広まったという。
summary_en: Rice cooked with roasted soybeans in brewed tea, said to have originated with Todai-ji's monks. Travelers are said to have carried it to Edo, where shops near Asakusa made it famous, while in Nara itself it is said to have only spread widely again from the Meiji era on.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Fuki dawara — salted rice and soybeans wrapped in butterbur leaves, offered at rice planting
summary_ja: 炒った大豆とご飯を塩味で炊き、ふきの葉で包んだ大和高原地域のおにぎり。田植えの始まりを祝う「さびらき」に、苗とともに畦に供えてから食べるとされ、俵の形に似せて作ることからこの名がついた。
summary_en: A rice ball from the Yamato Highlands, made from rice cooked with roasted soybeans and salt, then wrapped in butterbur leaves. It is said to be set out along the paddy ridge beside the rice seedlings at sabiraki, the rite marking the start of planting, and shaped to resemble a straw rice bale, which gives it its name.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Mana mehari — a rice ball wrapped whole in salted Shimokita spring greens
summary_ja: 下北山村だけで栽培される大和の伝統野菜、下北春まなの塩漬けでご飯を包んだおにぎり。高菜を使う十津川地域のめはりずしと作り方は同じだが、辛みが少なくやや小ぶりとされ、山仕事の弁当として親しまれてきた。
summary_en: A rice ball wrapped in salted Shimokita spring greens, a traditional Yamato vegetable grown only in Shimokitayama Village. It is made the same way as the mustard-leaf mehari-zushi of the Totsukawa area but is said to be milder and somewhat smaller, and has long been carried as a lunch for mountain work.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Iro gohan — rice cooked with root vegetables in a soy-seasoned broth
summary_ja: ニンジンやゴボウ、薄揚げなどをだし汁と醤油で炊き込んだ、奈良で「色ご飯」と呼ばれる混ぜご飯。米が貴重だった頃、具を混ぜてかさを増やしたことが始まりとされ、村の行事や日々の食卓に登場してきた。
summary_en: A takikomi rice dish called iro gohan in Nara, cooked with carrot, burdock, and fried tofu in a soy-seasoned dashi. It is said to have begun as a way to stretch scarce rice by mixing in other ingredients, and appears both at village events and everyday tables.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
